text:
nora: Heads up — noticed p95 tail for short-chat models in eu-west starting ~02:40 UTC. spikes correlate with first-token latency. :frowning:
devin: saw that too. packet traces show large rx coalescing bursts and PCIe DMA queue depth spikes around the same time window.
devin: snippet from host dmesg + iostat: ```journal: nvme0n1 queue full, timeout
iostat: sda  r/s=0 w/s=0 avgrq-sz=512 await=85.3```
claire: are these nodes running fractional slices/mig? that can amplify context-switch NVMe flushes.
pete: yes, affected hosts are fractional-slice enabled and running mixed workloads (small gen + occasional large-batch training).
nora: temporary thought — can we limit background batchers on machines that host low-latency slices? like a classifier in allocator to mark hosts "low-noise" and avoid placing heavy i/o jobs.
devin: short-term mitigation: reduce eth0 rx-usecs and drop coalesce, RPS up. did a quick test on a single host and first-token dropped ~25%. command we used: ```sudo ethtool -C eth0 rx-usecs 125 rx-frames 1; echo 2048 > /sys/class/net/eth0/queues/rx-0/rps_cpus```
claire: +1. also consider setting nvme io scheduler to noop for those hosts and lowering queue_depth for heavy tenants.
pete: cost question — moving heavy jobs to dedicated warm-pools will consume capacity. how big of a carveout are we thinking?
nora: liaison suggested 3 nodes for eu-west for a 15m rolling window (ops-bot started that). low cost relative to SLA exposure.
ops-bot: autoscaler: warm-pool carveout requested by @nora — 3 nodes in eu-west started (job id: wp-cc-1708).
devin: longer-term: allocator needs a soft-affinity quiet-host signal derived from irq/dma metrics so packing avoids noisy hosts for latency-sensitive tenants. scoring could be: noise_score = alpha*irq_rate + beta*nvme_stalls + gamma*iops_of_background_jobs.
claire: that scoring makes sense. we should also integrate a cooldown to avoid flip-flopping when noisy sources are transient.
pete: can we add a preemptive fallback where, if quiet-host pool < threshold, allocator prefers dedicated-slice allocation instead of fractional? fallback cost model should be surfaced to cost team.
nora: action items: 1) ops: roll ethtool/rps + nvme noop on affected rack (devin) 2) ops-bot: keep warm-pool carveout for 1h and auto-shrink if stable (ops-bot) 3) infra: prototype quiet-host metric and expose to allocator (pete + claire) 4) cost: model fallback tradeoffs for dedicated fallback (nora to loop in finance).
devin: i'll push a 1-liner script and runbook entries for SRE to run during incidents.
claire: i'll start a small exporter to push irq/pcie/nvme counters into prometheus under infra.noise.* tags so we can backfill and tune alpha/beta/gamma.
pete: i'll mock the allocator patch that treats quiet-host as a soft constraint and share benchmark numbers for 10k placements.
nora: thanks all. keep updates here; if any host recovers we can scope down the carveout. :eyes:
